scenario: AITA for calling out professor for making fun of me in class? | Backstory real quick: (20M) I’m a ginger (orange hair, freckles, and I wear glasses as well) and have been made fun of for it for basically my whole life; I’ve had to hear just about every term in the book from firehead, red, carrot top, firecrotch, etc. All of it really pisses me off but I try to keep it to myself b/c god forbid people think I “can’t take a joke”. On several different occasions a professor I had in one of my tech classes this past semester made “jokes” about it. Second week of the year he says after forgetting my name “I’ll remember you, you’re the guy with no soul” and third week “Oh that’s right EverywhereForever, you’re the ginger with no soul”. Most of the class laughed, I was pissed and too embarrassed to say anything. It stopped for awhile after that though. Towards the end of the semester though he did it again, and I straight lost my cool and said “It’s not funny. How would you like it if I called you baldy every day I walked in?” He didn’t say anything, class was quiet and he just continued with his lesson. I left for the bathroom b/c I was embarrassed and just got it together and walked back into class like nothing happened. The next day a kid talks to me outside class and said I was a dick about it and I just shrugged. Far be it from me to think something as arbitrary as my fucking hair color would be beyond juvenile and insulting remarks in college. AITA for the way I had reacted to this? This was mostly younger kids who had just graduated last year I think so I guess it may have influence on how they think but I wouldn’t expect it from a professor.

In one of my tech classes last semester, a professor made jokes about my appearance on several occasions. The second week of the year, he forgot my name and said, "I'll remember you; you're the guy with no soul." The third week, he said, "Oh, that's right, *Everywhere Forever*, you're the ginger with no soul." Most of the class laughed, and I was pissed and too embarrassed to say anything. First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA stands for "Am I the Asshole?" It's a way to evaluate whether your actions or feelings in a particular situation are justified or if you're overreacting. In this case, I feel like I was being made fun of by a professor, which is someone in a position of authority. Being mocked in front of classmates is humiliating, especially when it's about something I can't change about myself, like my hair color. I tried to keep my cool at first, but when it happened again, I snapped. I told the professor it wasn't funny and compared it to being called bald every day. That's a valid point because it's about the consistency of the behavior and how it affects the person. However, I also understand that professors are human and might make offhand comments without realizing the impact. But in this case, it happened multiple times, which makes it more than just a one-off joke. I also need to consider the reaction of the class. Most of them laughed, which could mean they found it funny or were just following the professor's lead. The fact that a classmate later called me a dick for reacting suggests that some people didn't see the issue with the professor's comments. On the other hand, I have the right to feel respected in an academic environment. Making fun of a student's appearance, especially in front of others, crosses a line. It's not just about taking a joke; it's about creating a hostile learning environment. I also need to think about the power dynamics. A professor has authority over students, and using that position to mock someone can be intimidating and discouraging. It's important to address such behavior to maintain a respectful and inclusive classroom. In my reaction, I stood up for myself, which is commendable. However, the way I did it might have been confrontational. Maybe there's a more constructive way to address the issue, like talking to the professor privately or reporting it to higher authorities if it continues. But considering the immediate situation, I was in a classroom with the professor and classmates. Reacting in the moment was spontaneous, and I did it to stop the behavior. It's understandable that I felt the need to defend myself. I also need to reflect on how I felt afterward. I was embarrassed and went to the bathroom to compose myself. That shows that the incident had a significant emotional impact on me, which is valid. In summary, while I might have overreacted in the moment, my underlying feelings of being disrespected and humiliated are justified. The professor's repeated jokes about my appearance were inappropriate, and it's reasonable to want to address that behavior. However, I could have handled it differently to avoid confrontation, but given the circumstances, my reaction was a spontaneous defense mechanism. It's important to balance standing up for oneself with maintaining professionalism and seeking appropriate channels for addressing such issues in the future.
